clue.text: Advice for elderly leader: go quietly

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
for can stand for to, as in a toast for or to someone

indicators.note: the leader of the word elderly is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone tells an ageing chief that it is time to slip away without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elderly leader' looks like an old boss, but 'leader' only asks for the first letter of 'elderly', giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: To move on the points of your feet is how you walk without making a sound.

clue.text: Official has to lean on stick

parts.note: to tip is to lean or tilt
a staff is a walking stick or rod

explanation.surface: A functionary is obliged to rest his weight on a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a court officer, named after the metal-tipped staff once carried as a badge of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A court officer or bailiff, historically carrying a tipped staff as a mark of authority.

clue.text: Discovery guarded in France

explanation.surface: Something found was kept safe somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A talented newcomer taken up and promoted by a patron; in French the word literally means protected.

clue.text: Exaggerated past oppresses Haggard

indicators.note: oppresses means weighs down from above, so in this down clue the word for past sits on top

parts.note: over means past or finished
drawn means haggard, looking strained and tired

explanation.surface: An overstated history bears down heavily on a man named Haggard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' with its capital looks like a name (the novelist Rider Haggard), but means DRAWN; 'oppresses' puts OVER above it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account overdrawn is in debit; a portrait or account overdrawn is overstated.

clue.text: Wide clearing

explanation.surface: A broad stretch of open land in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means broad or far-reaching (a wide view); it is also the act of clearing a floor with a brush.

clue.text: Oil fire believed doused? That's carefully planned

explanation.surface: Reporting that a blaze at an oil site is thought to be out, after careful planning.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic reading: an oil-well fire might be thought out, meaning believed extinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as well (oil source), thought (believed) and out (extinguished); as a phrase it means fully considered.

clue.text: Peak moves off top of counter

indicators.note: moves off top of tells us to take away the first letter of the word for counter

parts.note: a Geiger counter detects radiation

explanation.surface: A mountain shifts away from the top of a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a shop surface, but means GEIGER, from the Geiger counter; drop its first letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Alpine mountain in Switzerland, known for its north face.

clue.text: He takes for granted location of fire

explanation.surface: A man who assumes things will be given, beside the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person takes kindness for granted; read as two words, a fire burns in a grate.

clue.text: On the uptake, prisoner to cut and run

indicators.note: on the uptake means going upwards, which in a down clue turns the word for prisoner backwards

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, an old lag
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A convict quickly understanding his chance to cut loose and flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the uptake' sounds like quick understanding, but in this down entry it reverses LAG to GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest pace; to go at that pace is to ride or move very fast.

clue.text: Old guard pronounced towns in strange ways

indicators.note: pronounced means said aloud, so the words for old guard are taken as they sound

parts.note: an ex-sentry is a guard of old, a former sentry
cities are large towns

explanation.surface: Veteran guards spoke of urban places having odd habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old guard' looks like the established elite, but means a former sentry, EX-SENTRY, which sounds like ECCENTRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd habits or quirks of behaviour are a person's peculiarities.

clue.text: Established state language

parts.note: proven means shown to be true, established
Cal is a short form for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A statement that a recognised country has its own official tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Established state' reads as a settled nation, but splits into PROVEN plus CAL, an abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romance tongue of southern France, Occitan, takes its name from the region of Provence.

clue.text: He wrote about II Kings

annotationWithheld.why: He wrote about II Kings (5): GOGOL; GOG and OG are two biblical kings but give GOGOG, and no clue word supplies the final L, so no honest parse found

clue.text: Pedal is altered, being plastic

indicators.note: plastic means easily moulded into a new shape, so the letters of altered are reshaped

explanation.surface: A foot control has been changed because it is made of a mouldable material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being plastic' reads as the pedal's material, but it is the anagram signal working on 'altered'.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated lever, as on an old sewing machine or loom, that drives a wheel.

clue.text: For sailors, here's trouble

parts.note: for can stand for to, as in a gift for or to someone
RN is the Royal Navy, the British fleet of sailors
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A warning that bad times lie ahead for those at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: TO, RN and ADO join up, and a violent whirlwind is indeed trouble for sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is a serious danger to any vessel caught at sea.

clue.text: Geoffrey, amorously embracing love goddess

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the run of letters sits within Geoffrey, amorously

explanation.surface: A man named Geoffrey lovingly hugs a woman he adores as a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' looks like Geoffrey's romantic gesture, but signals letters held inside 'Geoffrey, amorously'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth she is the deity of love, beauty and fertility.

clue.text: Young swimmer allowed to follow the crowd? Not he

indicators.note: follow tells us the word for allowed comes after the rest
Not tells us to drop the word he from the word just before it

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A youngster is permitted to go along with everyone else, except that he is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not he' takes HE from 'the', leaving T; then comes ROUT, an old word for a crowd, and LET follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A small young fish of the salmon family is a little trout.

clue.text: Revolutionary met horrid time in Paris then

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the letters of met and horrid are turned around

explanation.surface: A rebel had a dreadful time in the French capital back in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a person, but signals the anagram; the answer is also a month of the French Revolutionary calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month of the French Republican calendar, roughly mid-July to mid-August.

clue.text: Oh dear, girl is trapped in the boot

indicators.note: is trapped in means caught inside, so the girl's name goes inside the word for boot

parts.note: a welly is a wellington, a rubber boot
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay because a young woman is stuck in the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the boot' suggests a car's luggage space, but it is a WELLY, a British rubber boot; ADA goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation of sorrow, like alas.

clue.text: Ruler of the birds, being a peacock?

explanation.surface: Asking whether the monarch of the bird world is the showy one with the tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A king of the swans would rule those birds; swanking is showing off, which a strutting peacock does.

clue.text: Scarlet's claim to be sweet, maybe

explanation.surface: Someone named Scarlet insists that she is nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Scarlet of the Robin Hood legend might say 'Will I am'; sweet william is a garden flower.

clue.text: Bird that is inferior to this one, of course

definitions.text: Bird that is inferior to this one, of course

parts.words: Bird that is inferior to this one, of course
parts.note: on a golf course a birdie is one under par, worse than the score two under par named after a bigger bird

explanation.surface: A remark that one bird obviously ranks below another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' seems to mean 'naturally', but it points to the golf course, where scores are named after birds.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, two strokes under par beats a birdie, which is only one under.

clue.text: Mystic allowing finally almost no criticism

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word allowing
almost means nearly all, so the last letter of the word for criticism is dropped

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: A spiritual person permits hardly any disapproval at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: G (the end of 'allowing') + NO + STIC, from STICK, British slang for criticism, with 'almost' cutting its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of an early sect claiming secret spiritual knowledge.

clue.text: It may provide calories, so put aside

indicators.note: put aside means set apart, so the letters of so are taken away and the rest rearranged

explanation.surface: Something fattening, so leave it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of 'so' out of 'calories' and rearrange the rest, CALRIE, to get the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream-filled choux pastry topped with chocolate is fattening.

clue.text: Very large figures for waste in Government publicity service

indicators.note: in tells us the word for waste goes inside the letters for the service

parts.note: COI was the Central Office of Information, the UK government's publicity agency
loss means waste, something wasted

explanation.surface: Big numbers spent on waste by the official agency that handles government advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' suggests money, but means statues; COI was Britain's Central Office of Information.
explanation.definitionFit: These are giant statues, like the one that stood over the harbour at Rhodes.

clue.text: Greek statesman's farewell cut short

indicators.note: cut short means losing its end, so the last letter of the word for farewell goes

parts.note: so long is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: An ancient Athenian politician says a brief goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: SO LONG, an informal goodbye, loses its last letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian lawgiver of the sixth century BC, whose name now means a wise legislator.

clue.text: Silly characters in Lear

parts.note: Edgar disguises himself as Poor Tom in Shakespeare's King Lear
the Fool is the king's jester in Shakespeare's King Lear

explanation.surface: A remark that the people in Shakespeare's tragedy are ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like letters, but means two people in King Lear: Poor Tom and the Fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it means foolish or absurd.

clue.text: Spirit kept twelve years in pine

definitions.text: Spirit kept twelve years in pine

parts.words: Spirit kept twelve years in pine
parts.note: in The Tempest the witch Sycorax shut a sprite inside a cloven pine tree for twelve years until Prospero freed it

explanation.surface: A drink aged for twelve years in wooden casks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit kept twelve years' suggests aged whisky, but the spirit is the sprite of Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play this airy sprite serves Prospero after he frees it from the tree.

clue.text: Overwhelmed United and went wild

indicators.note: went wild means ran out of control, so the letters of United and and are scrambled

explanation.surface: A football team was swamped and its fans or players lost control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club, but it and 'and' are rearranged, signalled by 'went wild'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooded or swamped, as by water or by too much work.

clue.text: A sermon I arranged to submit to the Vatican

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of a sermon I are reordered

explanation.surface: A preacher says he has prepared a sermon to send to the Pope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like the sermon being organised, but signals that the letters of 'A sermon I' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a person or church under Roman Catholic authority, whose centre is in Rome.

clue.text: Dear, sweet, without peer

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the letters for peer go around the others

parts.note: to pry is to peer nosily
an ice is a frozen sweet or dessert

explanation.surface: A loving address to a darling who has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without peer' reads as 'unequalled', but 'without' means outside: PRY goes around ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly; something expensive is said to be dear.
